title: Degenerate tiling incidence conjecture over division rings
statement: Let $\mathcal T$ be a **simple tiling** of a surface of positive genus, meaning that its underlying graph is $(n+1)$-degenerate, and let ${\mathrm D}$ be a division ring. The incidence theorem corresponding to $\mathcal T$ is an incidence statement in projective space $\mathbb{P}^n({\mathrm D})$. **Degenerate tiling incidence conjecture.** The incidence theorem corresponding to $\mathcal T$ holds in $\mathbb{P}^n({\mathrm D})$ if and only if ${\mathrm D}$ is commutative. This would extend the preceding argument from the specific tiling considered there to all simple $(n+1)$-degenerate tilings of positive-genus surfaces; combined with bounds on the degeneracy of graphs embeddable in a fixed genus, it would imply corresponding dimension thresholds for all simple tilings of a fixed positive genus.
source_name: Anton Izosimov, “Surface topology and incidence theorems over division rings”, arXiv:2603.00288 (2026).
